intro: At the edge of the excavation stands the Aphrodisias Museum, in Aydın province, opened in 1979. Inside you will meet the work of the city's school of sculptors, and one hall is given entirely to the Sebasteion reliefs.
history: By 1979 the excavations had produced more sculpture than the town could hold, so the museum was built at the edge of the site. The marble quarry was two kilometres away, and the city's school of sculptors supplied the empire. Here, their work stays where it was made.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the Sebasteion reliefs and the finds from the sculpture workshops. Pause before the statues of Aphrodite, and spend time with the unfinished pieces.
facts: Did you know? The most instructive pieces here are the unfinished ones: a single row shows every stage a Roman statue passed through, from rough block to polish. The marble quarry lay two kilometres from the city, and the signatures of its sculptors turn up from Rome to North Africa.
outro: Our time in the Aphrodisias Museum ends here. One small request before you go: please leave the objects untouched and take your photographs without flash, so these pieces stay safe for the visitors who follow you. Thank you for listening, and enjoy your visit.
